title.zh: 卷483 列傳二百七十 儒林四 孔荫植子：兴燮 毓圻子：傳铎 广棨子：昭焕 孙：宪培 曾孙：庆镕 曾孙：繁灏 玄孙：祥珂 来孙：令贻
title.en: Volume 483 Biographies 270: Confucian Scholars 4: Kong Yinzhi Son: Xing Xie, Yu Qi Son: Chuan Duo, Guang Qi Son: Zhao Huan, Sun :Xianpei, Zeng Sun : Qing Rong, Zeng Sun : Fan Hao, Xuan Sun : Xiang Ke, Lai Sun : Ling Yi
title.raw: 卷483 列傳二百七十 儒林四 孔荫植子：兴燮 毓圻子：傳铎 广棨子：昭焕 孙：宪培 曾孙：庆镕 曾孙：繁灏 玄孙：祥珂 来孙：令贻

sentences.zh: 列傳二百七十

translations.literal: Biographies 270
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 270

sentences.zh: 儒林四

translations.literal: Confucian Scholars 4
translations.idiomatic: Confucian Scholars 4

sentences.zh: 孔廕植

translations.literal: Kong Yinzhi
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yinzhi

sentences.zh: 孔廕植，字對寰，孔子六十五代孫，世居曲阜。

translations.literal: Kong Yinzhi, style name Duihuan, was a sixty-fifth-generation descendant of Confucius whose family had long resided in Qufu.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yinzhi, whose style was Duihuan, was a sixty-fifth-generation descendant of Confucius and came from a family that had long lived in Qufu.

sentences.zh: 明天啟初，襲封衍聖公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign of the Ming, he inherited the title Duke Yansheng.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Ming Tianqi reign, he inherited the dukedom of Yansheng.

sentences.zh: 清順治元年，世祖定鼎京師，山東巡撫方大猷疏言開國之初，首宜尊崇先聖。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi of the Qing, when the Founding Emperor established the capital at Beijing, the Shandong provincial governor Fang Dayou memorialized that at the opening of a dynasty one should first honor the ancient sage.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shunzhi, after the Founding Emperor had fixed the capital at Beijing, Shandong governor Fang Dayou submitted a memorial arguing that at the founding of a dynasty the ancient sage ought to be honored first.

sentences.zh: 下禮部議，衍聖公爵及其官屬，悉循明舊制。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the Ministry of Rites for deliberation; the Duke Yansheng and all his subordinate officials were to follow entirely the former Ming regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The case was sent to the Ministry of Rites, which ruled that the Duke Yansheng and his entire staff should continue under the Ming arrangements unchanged.

sentences.zh: 廕植朝京師，遣官迎勞。

translations.literal: When Yinzhi came to the capital, officials were dispatched to welcome and comfort him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yinzhi traveled to the capital, the court sent officials to welcome him and attend to his comfort.

sentences.zh: 入朝，班列大學士上，賜宴，恩禮有加。

translations.literal: On entering court he was ranked above the grand secretaries, was granted a banquet, and received added favor and ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: At court he was placed in the procession above the grand secretaries, given a banquet, and treated with exceptional courtesy.

sentences.zh: 四年，卒，遣山東布政使致祭。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died; the Shandong provincial administration commissioner was sent to perform the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year, and the Shandong provincial administration commissioner was dispatched to offer sacrifice on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 子興燮襲。

translations.literal: His son Xing Xie succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xing Xie succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 興燮，字起呂。

translations.literal: Xing Xie, style name Qilü.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Xie, whose style was Qilü.

sentences.zh: 時年十三，生母陶撫以成立。

translations.literal: He was then thirteen years old; his birth mother, née Tao, reared him until he came of age.
translations.idiomatic: He was only thirteen; his birth mother, Lady Tao, raised him until he reached maturity.

sentences.zh: 稍長，事母甚孝，凝重有器識。

translations.literal: When he grew somewhat older he was extremely filial toward his mother, grave in bearing, and possessed of capacity and judgment.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew older he showed deep filial devotion to his mother, carried himself with weight and composure, and displayed real judgment and presence of mind.

sentences.zh: 飭廟庭，修禮樂，諸廢悉舉。

translations.literal: He put the temple precinct in order, restored ritual and music, and revived every abandoned practice.
translations.idiomatic: He restored discipline in the temple compound, renewed the ritual music, and brought back every practice that had fallen into disuse.

sentences.zh: 累加少保兼太子太保。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Junior Guardian and concurrently Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted repeatedly until he held the ranks of Junior Guardian and Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent concurrently.

sentences.zh: 康熙六年，卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kangxi he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year of the Kangxi reign.

sentences.zh: 子毓圻襲。

translations.literal: His son Yu Qi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yu Qi succeeded.

sentences.zh: 毓圻，字鐘在。

translations.literal: Yu Qi, style name Zhongzai.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qi, whose style was Zhongzai.

sentences.zh: 方幼，年十一，朝京師。

translations.literal: While still young, at age eleven, he came to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Still a child, he went to the capital at the age of eleven.

sentences.zh: 聖祖召見瀛台，禮度如成人，奏對稱旨。

translations.literal: The Holy Ancestor summoned him to an audience at Yingtai; his deportment was like that of an adult, and his replies to the throne accorded with the Emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: The Kangxi Emperor received him at Yingtai; he conducted himself with the poise of a grown man, and everything he said in audience pleased the throne.

sentences.zh: 越二年，上幸學，召毓圻陪祀，太皇太后召入見，賜坐，問家世，具以對，賜茶及克食。

translations.literal: Two years later, when the Emperor visited the Imperial Academy, Yu Qi was summoned to assist at the sacrifice; the Grand Empress Dowager summoned him in for an audience, granted him a seat, inquired about his family history, and he answered in full detail; she bestowed tea and traveling provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later, when the Emperor attended the Imperial Academy rites, Yu Qi was called to assist at the sacrifice. The Grand Empress Dowager summoned him in, gave him a seat, and asked about his lineage; he answered at length, and she granted him tea and provisions for the road.

sentences.zh: 辭出，命內臣送至宮門外，傳諭從官善輔翼之。

translations.literal: When he took leave to withdraw, she ordered inner attendants to escort him to the palace gate; an edict was transmitted instructing his attendants to guide and support him well.
translations.idiomatic: As he withdrew, she ordered palace eunuchs to escort him to the outer gate and sent word that his attendants should guide and support him carefully.

sentences.zh: 上御殿，毓圻從諸大臣朝參，及退，命自御道行，逡巡辭，上敦諭之，乃趨出。

translations.literal: When the Emperor held court, Yu Qi followed the great ministers in paying homage; when they retired, the Emperor ordered him to walk by the imperial roadway; hesitating, he declined, but the Emperor urged him earnestly, whereupon he hastened out.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor held audience, Yu Qi joined the senior ministers in obeisance; as they withdrew, the Emperor told him to use the imperial path. He hesitated and demurred, but the Emperor pressed him firmly, and he then hurried out.

sentences.zh: 加太子少師。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，上東巡，釋奠孔子廟，留曲柄黃蓋。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year the Emperor made an eastern tour, performed the libation sacrifice at the Temple of Confucius, and left behind a curved-handled yellow canopy.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year the Emperor toured the east, offered libation at the Temple of Confucius, and left behind a curved-handled yellow imperial canopy as a mark of honor.

sentences.zh: 謁林，週覽遺跡，每事問，毓圻謹以對。

translations.literal: He visited the Kong Forest, surveyed the historic sites all around, and questioned him on every matter; Yu Qi answered with care.
translations.idiomatic: He visited the Kong Forest and went through the historic sites, questioning him on each point; Yu Qi answered with scrupulous care.

sentences.zh: 因請擴林地，置守衛，除租賦，設百戶，官秩視衛守備，皆許之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he requested expansion of the forest grounds, establishment of guards, exemption from rent and tax, and the setting up of a hundred households, with official rank equal to a garrison commandant; all were granted.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked to enlarge the forest estate, post guards, lift rent and tax obligations, and establish a corps of a hundred households with rank equivalent to a garrison commandant; the Emperor approved every request.

sentences.zh: 毓圻輯幸魯盛典以進，復奏請重修孔子廟，白巡撫及河道總督，免縣人河工應役。

translations.literal: Yu Qi compiled the record of the Emperor's visit to Lu and presented it; he also memorialized requesting reconstruction of the Temple of Confucius, informed the provincial governor and the Grand Canal director-general, and secured exemption for county people from corvée on river works.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qi edited the account of the imperial visit to Lu and presented it to the throne. He also memorialized for the rebuilding of the Confucius temple, secured the support of the provincial governor and the Grand Canal director-general, and obtained exemption for the people of the county from river-labor corvée.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，世宗命追封先聖五代王爵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng the Shizong Emperor ordered posthumous ennoblement of the ancient sage's five generations as kings.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongzheng, the Yongzheng Emperor ordered that five generations of the ancient sage be ennobled posthumously as kings.

sentences.zh: 十月，毓圻詣闕謝，疾作，上命醫診視，賜參餌。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Yu Qi came to court to give thanks; illness seized him; the Emperor ordered physicians to examine him and bestowed ginseng medicine.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Yu Qi came to court to offer thanks; he fell ill, and the Emperor ordered physicians to attend him and sent ginseng as medicine.

sentences.zh: 十一月，卒於京師，上遣內大臣奠茶酒。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he died in the capital; the Emperor dispatched an inner grand minister to offer libations of tea and wine.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he died in the capital; the Emperor sent an inner grand minister to offer libations of tea and wine.

sentences.zh: 喪歸，命皇三子及莊親王允祿臨奠，行人護行，賜葬，諡恭愨。

translations.literal: When the coffin returned home, the Emperor ordered the third imperial son and Prince Zhuang Yunlu to attend the mourning rites, officials to escort the procession, granted burial honors, and conferred the posthumous title Gongmin.
translations.idiomatic: When his coffin returned home, the Emperor ordered the third imperial son and Prince Zhuang Yunlu to attend the mourning, sent officials to escort the procession, granted state burial, and gave him the posthumous title Gongmin.

sentences.zh: 毓圻工書，愛蘭，自號曰蘭堂。

translations.literal: Yu Qi was skilled at calligraphy, loved orchids, and styled himself the Orchid Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qi was accomplished in calligraphy, loved orchids, and took the sobriquet Orchid Hall.

sentences.zh: 子傳鐸襲。

translations.literal: His son Chuan Duo succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chuan Duo succeeded.

sentences.zh: 傳鐸，字振路。

translations.literal: Chuan Duo, style name Zhenlu.
translations.idiomatic: Chuan Duo, whose style was Zhenlu.

sentences.zh: 康熙間賜二品冠服，襲爵後一年，世宗幸學，召傳鐸陪祀。

translations.literal: During the Kangxi reign he was granted second-rank court dress; one year after succeeding to the title, when the Shizong visited the Imperial Academy, Chuan Duo was summoned to assist at the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kangxi reign he was granted second-rank court dress. One year after inheriting the title, when the Yongzheng Emperor visited the Imperial Academy, Chuan Duo was summoned to assist at the sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 傳鐸老，病足，命其子繼溥代行禮。

translations.literal: Chuan Duo was old and afflicted in the feet; the Emperor ordered his son Jibo to perform the rites in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: Chuan Duo was elderly and lame; the Emperor ordered his son Jibo to perform the rites on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 六月，孔子廟災，傳鐸用明弘治間故事，率族人素服三日哭，疏引咎，上遣侍郎王景曾祭告。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the Temple of Confucius suffered a fire; Chuan Duo followed the precedent of the Hongzhi reign of the Ming, led the clan in plain dress for three days of weeping, and submitted a memorial taking blame upon himself; the Emperor dispatched Vice Minister Wang Jingceng to perform the sacrificial announcement.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the Temple of Confucius caught fire. Chuan Duo followed the Ming Hongzhi precedent, led the clan in mourning dress for three days of weeping, and submitted a self-reproach memorial; the Emperor sent Vice Minister Wang Jingceng to announce the sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 並傳旨慰問。

translations.literal: An edict of consolation was also transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: An edict of consolation was sent as well.

sentences.zh: 尋發帑重建，命侍郎留保會巡撫岳濬、前巡撫陳世倌庀工役，而以傳鐸董其事。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter funds were issued from the treasury for reconstruction; the Emperor ordered Vice Minister Liubao to join with Governor Yue Jun and former governor Chen Shichang to arrange the labor, while Chuan Duo was put in overall charge.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward imperial funds were released for rebuilding; the Emperor ordered Vice Minister Liubao to work with Governor Yue Jun and former governor Chen Shichang in organizing the labor, while Chuan Duo supervised the project.

sentences.zh: 詔詢傳鐸，有當增設者言無隱。

translations.literal: An edict inquired of Chuan Duo, saying that whatever ought to be added he should speak of without concealment.
translations.idiomatic: An edict asked Chuan Duo to speak frankly of anything that ought to be added.

sentences.zh: 因請增設樂器庫直房，上許之。

translations.literal: He thereupon requested addition of a straight office for the musical-instrument storehouse; the Emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked for a direct office attached to the musical-instrument repository, and the Emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 八年，廟成。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the temple was completed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the temple was finished.

sentences.zh: 九年，上命修孔林，仍與世倌監理，疾作乞休，上允之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the Emperor ordered repair of the Kong Forest; he still supervised the work together with Shichang; when illness came on he begged to retire, and the Emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the Emperor ordered repairs to the Kong Forest; Chuan Duo continued to supervise the work with Chen Shichang. When illness set in he asked to retire, and the Emperor allowed it.

sentences.zh: 子繼濩前卒，命以孫廣棨襲。

translations.literal: His son Jihuo had died earlier; the Emperor ordered that his grandson Guang Qi succeed.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jihuo had died earlier, so the Emperor ordered his grandson Guang Qi to succeed.

sentences.zh: 十年，孔林工竟，復開館輯闕里盛典。

translations.literal: In the tenth year work on the Kong Forest was finished; the academy was reopened to compile the Queli ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year work on the Kong Forest was completed, and the academy was reopened to compile the ceremonial records of Queli.

sentences.zh: 十三年，卒，賜祭葬。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he died; state sacrifice and burial were granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he died, and state sacrifice and burial were granted.

sentences.zh: 傳鐸工詩詞，有集。

translations.literal: Chuan Duo was skilled in poetry and lyrics and left a collected works.
translations.idiomatic: Chuan Duo was skilled in poetry and song lyrics and left a collection of writings.

sentences.zh: 廣棨，字京立。

translations.literal: Guang Qi, style name Jingli.
translations.idiomatic: Guang Qi, whose style was Jingli.

sentences.zh: 雍正初，授二品冠服，襲爵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongzheng he was granted second-rank court dress and succeeded to the title.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongzheng reign he was granted second-rank court dress and inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 以孔林工竟，率族人詣闕謝。

translations.literal: Because work on the Kong Forest had been completed, he led the clan to court to give thanks.
translations.idiomatic: When the Kong Forest project was finished, he led the clan to court to offer thanks.

sentences.zh: 上御圓明園正大光明殿，召入對，命坐賜茶，諭曰：「汝為先聖後，當存聖賢心，行聖賢事，秉禮守義，以驕奢為戒。

translations.literal: The Emperor held audience in the Hall of Rectitude and Brightness in the Old Summer Palace, summoned him for an interview, ordered him to be seated and granted tea, and instructed him, saying: "You are a descendant of the ancient sage; you should keep the heart of the sages, perform the deeds of the sages, uphold ritual and guard righteousness, and take pride and extravagance as your warning.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor received him in the Hall of Rectitude and Brightness at the Old Summer Palace, summoned him for audience, had him seated, and granted tea. He instructed him: "As a descendant of the ancient sage, you must keep the sages' heart, do the sages' deeds, hold to ritual and righteousness, and guard against pride and luxury.

sentences.zh: 汝年方少，尤宜勤學讀書，敦品勵行，與汝族人相勸戒，相砥礪，為端人正士。」

translations.literal: You are still very young; you should all the more study diligently and read books, cultivate character and encourage conduct, and with your clansmen admonish and restrain one another, polish one another, and become upright gentlemen."
translations.idiomatic: You are still very young, and should study and read all the more diligently, cultivate your character, encourage one another among your kinsmen, and become upright, principled men."

sentences.zh: 廣棨頓首謝。

translations.literal: Guang Qi bowed his head in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Guang Qi kowtowed in thanks.

sentences.zh: 賜松花江石硯及錦幣，賜宴，遣歸。

translations.literal: He was granted an inkstone of Songhua River stone and brocade silks, given a banquet, and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: He was given a Songhua River inkstone and brocade silks, entertained at banquet, and sent home.

sentences.zh: 十三年，世宗崩，入臨。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the Shizong died; he entered the capital to mourn.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the Yongzheng Emperor died, and he came to the capital to mourn.

sentences.zh: 高宗復召入對，以覃恩贈父繼濩如其爵。

translations.literal: The Gaozong Emperor again summoned him for an audience; because of a general amnesty his father Jihuo was posthumously ennobled to the same rank as his own title.
translations.idiomatic: The Qianlong Emperor summoned him again for audience and, under a general amnesty, posthumously ennobled his father Jihuo to the same rank as his own title.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三年，上幸學，召廣棨陪祀。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qianlong the Emperor visited the Imperial Academy and summoned Guang Qi to assist at the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Qianlong the Emperor visited the Imperial Academy and summoned Guang Qi to assist at the sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 獻親耕耤田頌、視學大禮慶成賦。

translations.literal: He presented an ode on the Emperor's plowing of the sacred field and a fu on the completion of the great ceremony of the imperial school visit.
translations.idiomatic: He presented an ode on the Emperor's ceremonial plowing of the sacred field and a fu celebrating the completion of the imperial school visit.

sentences.zh: 四年，朝京師，祝上萬壽。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he came to the capital to congratulate the Emperor on his birthday.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he came to the capital to congratulate the Emperor on his longevity.

sentences.zh: 會舉經筵，令侍班，因奏請著為令。

translations.literal: When the classics lecture was held, he was ordered to attend in the lecturing corps; he thereupon memorialized requesting that this be made a standing regulation.
translations.idiomatic: When the classics lecture was convened, he was ordered to attend in the lecturing corps and memorialized that the practice be made permanent.

sentences.zh: 六年，疏劾曲阜知縣毓琚不職，毓琚亦訐廣棨居鄉不法，下巡撫按治，上原廣棨而譴毓琚。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he memorialized impeaching Qufu magistrate Yu Ju for malfeasance; Yu Ju also denounced Guang Qi for unlawful conduct in his home district; the matter was sent to the governor for investigation; the Emperor excused Guang Qi and censured Yu Ju.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he memorialized against Qufu magistrate Yu Ju for dereliction of duty. Yu Ju in turn accused Guang Qi of misconduct at home. The case was sent to the provincial governor for investigation; the Emperor excused Guang Qi and punished Yu Ju.

sentences.zh: 八年，卒。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth year.

sentences.zh: 子昭煥襲。

translations.literal: His son Zhao Huan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhao Huan succeeded.

sentences.zh: 昭煥，字顯明，十三年正月，上東巡，釋奠孔子廟，禦詩禮堂。

translations.literal: Zhao Huan, style name Xianming; in the first month of the thirteenth year the Emperor made an eastern tour, performed the libation sacrifice at the Temple of Confucius, and visited the Hall of Poetry and Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Huan, whose style was Xianming. In the first month of the thirteenth year the Emperor toured the east, offered libation at the Temple of Confucius, and visited the Hall of Poetry and Rites.

sentences.zh: 昭煥方幼，命其族人舉人繼汾等進講。

translations.literal: Zhao Huan was still young; the Emperor ordered his kinsman, the presented scholar Jifen, and others to advance and lecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Huan was still a child, so the Emperor ordered his kinsman, presented scholar Jifen, and others to lecture in his place.

sentences.zh: 是日並謁林，還，复留曲柄黃蓋。

translations.literal: That same day he also visited the forest; on returning he again left behind a curved-handled yellow canopy.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he also visited the Kong Forest; on his return he again left a curved-handled yellow canopy.

sentences.zh: 賜昭煥宴，賚書籍、文綺、貂幣，官繼汾中書，族人有官者皆進秩。

translations.literal: He granted Zhao Huan a banquet and bestowed books, patterned silks, and sable gifts; Jifen was appointed Central Secretariat official, and every clansman who held office was promoted in rank.
translations.idiomatic: He gave Zhao Huan a banquet and bestowed books, brocades, and sable gifts. Jifen was appointed to the Central Secretariat, and every clansman in office received a promotion.

sentences.zh: 親制孔子廟碑，勒石大成門外。

translations.literal: The Emperor personally composed the stele for the Temple of Confucius and had it carved in stone outside the Gate of Great Accomplishment.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor personally composed the temple stele and had it engraved in stone outside the Gate of Great Accomplishment.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，昭煥疏言：「皇莊戶丁蒙恩免役，歷來地方官額外雜派，每事調劑非易，請酌留五十戶，餘改歸民籍，交地方官編審應役。」

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year Zhao Huan memorialized, saying: "The householders of the official estate have received the grace of exemption from corvée, yet over the years local officials have imposed extra miscellaneous levies, and it is not easy to adjust every matter; I request that fifty households be retained as appropriate, while the rest be transferred to commoner registration and handed to local officials for compilation and corvée assignment."
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year Zhao Huan memorialized: "The estate households have been graciously exempted from corvée, yet local officials have long imposed extra levies on them, making every adjustment difficult. I ask that fifty households be kept, while the rest be returned to the common register and assigned corvée by the local magistrate."

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「昭煥疏言皇莊，此必沿前代舊習，然亦止應稱官莊。

translations.literal: The Emperor instructed, saying: "In Zhao Huan's memorial he speaks of an imperial estate; this must be a habit carried over from earlier dynasties, yet he should only have called it the official estate.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Zhao Huan writes of an 'imperial estate'—no doubt an old habit from earlier dynasties—but he should have called it only the official estate.

sentences.zh: 子不云乎：'甚矣由之行詐，無臣而為有臣。

translations.literal: Did not the Master say: 'How excessive was the conduct of You in his deceit—having no minister yet acting as though he had one?
translations.idiomatic: Did not the Master say, 'How excessive was You in his deceit—having no minister yet acting as if he had one'?

sentences.zh: '昭煥可謂不能讀其祖書矣。

translations.literal: Zhao Huan can be said not to have read his ancestor's books.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Huan plainly has not read his ancestor's books.

sentences.zh: 此時丁銀已停徵，地方官安得更令百姓應役？

translations.literal: At this time the poll tax in silver had already ceased to be collected; how could local officials further make the common people perform corvée?
translations.idiomatic: By then the poll tax in silver had already been stopped; how could local officials still press the common people into corvée?

sentences.zh: 且取役何事？

translations.literal: Moreover, for what purpose was corvée to be taken?
translations.idiomatic: And for what work was corvée needed in the first place?

sentences.zh: 若為朕東巡修道，則皆發帑僱役，初未累百姓。

translations.literal: If it was for repairing roads on my eastern tour, all labor was hired with funds from the treasury and had never burdened the people from the start.
translations.idiomatic: If it was for repairing roads on my eastern tour, all labor was hired from the treasury and never fell on the people at all.

sentences.zh: 朕展謁先師，衍聖公督令廟戶除道清產，理所應爾，豈當轉庇廟戶，並發帑僱役亦不肯應耶？」

translations.literal: When I paid my respects to the ancient teacher, it was only right that the Duke Yansheng should supervise the temple households in clearing the roads and cleaning the grounds; how could he turn instead to shield the temple households, so that even hired labor from the treasury they would not supply?"
translations.idiomatic: When I visited the ancient teacher, it was only fitting that the Duke Yansheng should have the temple households clear the roads and clean the grounds. How could he instead shield those households, refusing even labor paid from the treasury?"

sentences.zh: 下吏議，當奪爵，上命寬之。

translations.literal: The officials deliberated and ruled that his title should be stripped; the Emperor ordered leniency.
translations.idiomatic: The officials recommended stripping his title, but the Emperor ordered leniency.

sentences.zh: 以昭煥年少，歸咎繼汾及其兄繼涑，皆譴黜。

translations.literal: Because Zhao Huan was young, blame was assigned to Jifen and his elder brother Jisu; both were punished and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zhao Huan was young, blame fell on Jifen and his elder brother Jisu; both were censured and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 三月，上東巡，釋奠孔子廟，謁林。

translations.literal: In the third month the Emperor made an eastern tour, performed the libation sacrifice at the Temple of Confucius, and visited the forest.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the Emperor toured the east, offered libation at the Temple of Confucius, and visited the Kong Forest.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，上奉皇太后東巡釋奠。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year the Emperor, accompanying the Empress Dowager, toured the east and performed the libation sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year the Emperor, with the Empress Dowager, toured the east and offered libation.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，復東巡釋奠。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year he again toured the east and performed the libation sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-sixth year he again toured the east and offered libation.

sentences.zh: 既還京師，出內府所藏週銅器木鼎、亞尊、犧尊、伯彝、冊卣、蟠夔敦、寶簠、夔鳳豆、饕餮甗、四足鬲，凡十事，置廟庭。

translations.literal: After returning to the capital, he brought out from the inner palace ten Zhou bronze vessels—the wooden ding, the ya vessel, the sacrificial zun, the Bo yi, the ce you, the coiled kui dun, the precious gui, the kui-phoenix dou, the taotie yan, and the four-legged li—and placed them in the temple court.
translations.idiomatic: After returning to the capital, he took from the inner palace ten Zhou bronzes—the wooden ding, ya zun, sacrificial zun, Bo yi, ce you, coiled kui dun, precious gui, kui-phoenix dou, taotie yan, and four-legged li—and set them in the temple courtyard.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，兩金川平。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year the two Jinchuan campaigns were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year the two Jinchuan campaigns were pacified.

sentences.zh: 三月，复奉皇太后東巡釋奠，告成功。

translations.literal: In the third month he again accompanied the Empress Dowager on an eastern tour to perform the libation sacrifice and announce the victory.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he again accompanied the Empress Dowager on an eastern tour to offer libation and announce the victory.

sentences.zh: 次日，謁林。

translations.literal: The next day he visited the forest.
translations.idiomatic: The following day he visited the Kong Forest.

sentences.zh: 四十八年，昭煥卒，子憲培襲。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year Zhao Huan died; his son Xian Pei succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-eighth year Zhao Huan died; his son Xian Pei succeeded.

sentences.zh: 憲培，字養元。

translations.literal: Xian Pei, style name Yangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xian Pei, whose style was Yangyuan.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十九年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year of Qianlong he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifty-ninth year of Qianlong.

sentences.zh: 子慶鎔襲。

translations.literal: His son Qing Rong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qing Rong succeeded.

sentences.zh: 慶鎔，字陶甫。

translations.literal: Qing Rong, style name Taofu.
translations.idiomatic: Qing Rong, whose style was Taofu.

sentences.zh: 道光二十一年，卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Daoguang he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-first year of Daoguang.

sentences.zh: 子繁灝襲。

translations.literal: His son Fan Hao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fan Hao succeeded.

sentences.zh: 繁灝，字文淵。

translations.literal: Fan Hao, style name Wenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Hao, whose style was Wenyuan.

sentences.zh: 同治二年，卒，諡端恪。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongzhi he died; his posthumous title was Duanke.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Tongzhi and received the posthumous title Duanke.

sentences.zh: 子祥珂襲。

translations.literal: His son Xiang Ke succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiang Ke succeeded.

sentences.zh: 祥珂，字覲堂。

translations.literal: Xiang Ke, style name Jintang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Ke, whose style was Jintang.

sentences.zh: 光緒三年，卒，諡莊愨。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guangxu he died; his posthumous title was Zhuangmin.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Guangxu and received the posthumous title Zhuangmin.

sentences.zh: 子令貽襲。

translations.literal: His son Ling Yi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ling Yi succeeded.

sentences.zh: 令貽，字穀孫。

translations.literal: Ling Yi, style name Gusun.
translations.idiomatic: Ling Yi, whose style was Gusun.

sentences.zh: 國變後，襲爵，奉祀如故。

translations.literal: After the change of dynasties he inherited the title and continued to perform sacrifices as before.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of the dynasty he inherited the title and carried on the sacrifices unchanged.

sentences.zh: 當唐末五季，以文宣公兼曲阜令。

translations.literal: At the end of Tang and through the Five Dynasties, the Duke of Wenxuan also held the post of Qufu magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: From the late Tang through the Five Dynasties, the Duke of Wenxuan had also served concurrently as magistrate of Qufu.

sentences.zh: 宋用孔氏支子，明至清初因之。

translations.literal: The Song employed a collateral line of the Kong clan, and the Ming through early Qing followed the same practice.
translations.idiomatic: The Song appointed a collateral branch of the Kong house, and the Ming through early Qing kept the same arrangement.

sentences.zh: 自毓琚與廣棨互訐坐罷官，廷議以衍聖公諮送易涉私，孔氏子領鄉縣，所隸皆親屬，審斷亦未能悉公，擬更前例。

translations.literal: After Yu Ju and Guang Qi denounced each other and were dismissed from office, court discussion held that when the Duke Yansheng forwarded nominations it was easy to involve private interest; when a Kong clansman headed the district and subordinates were all kin, judgments too could not be wholly impartial—so they proposed changing the former precedent.
translations.idiomatic: After Yu Ju and Guang Qi impeached each other and lost their posts, the court argued that when the Duke Yansheng forwarded nominations private favor was too easily involved, and that when a Kong clansman governed the county with kinsmen as subordinates judgments could hardly be fully impartial; they therefore proposed altering the old practice.

sentences.zh: 御史衛廷璞疏言宜仍舊貫，鴻臚寺卿林令旭又請以衢州孔氏子孫為曲阜知縣，下廷臣議，用廷璞言，仍令衍聖公諮送，巡撫考試題補。

translations.literal: Censor Wei Tingpu memorialized that the old practice should be kept; Grand Secretariat of State Ceremonies Lin Lingxu also asked that a descendant of the Quzhou Kong line serve as Qufu magistrate. The matter was referred to the court for deliberation; Tingpu's view was adopted, and the Duke Yansheng was still to forward nominations while the provincial governor examined candidates and appointed by imperial topic.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wei Tingpu memorialized that the old custom should stand; Director of the Court of State Ceremonies Lin Lingxu also asked that a descendant of the Quzhou Kong line be made Qufu magistrate. The case went to the full court, which followed Tingpu: the Duke Yansheng would still forward names, and the provincial governor would examine candidates and fill the post by imperial appointment.

sentences.zh: 後十餘年，巡撫白鍾山奏請改題缺。

translations.literal: More than ten years later, Governor Bai Zhongshan memorialized requesting that the post be changed to a regular provincial appointment.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten years later, Governor Bai Zhongshan memorialized to make the magistracy an ordinary provincial post.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「闕里毓聖之鄉，唐、宋以來，率以聖裔領縣事。

translations.literal: The Emperor instructed: "Queli is the village that nurtured the sage; since Tang and Song times the sage's descendants have generally held the district office.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Queli is the village that nurtured the sage; since Tang and Song, sage-descendants have usually held the county office.

sentences.zh: 大宗主鬯，爵列上公。

translations.literal: The great lineage presides over the sacrificial libation; its rank stands among the highest dukes.
translations.idiomatic: The main line presides over the libation wine, and its rank stands among the highest dukes.

sentences.zh: 而知縣以民事為職，奉法令，則以裁制傷恩；

translations.literal: Yet the magistrate's duty is the people's affairs; if he upholds the law, kinship is wounded by restraint;
translations.idiomatic: Yet a magistrate's charge is the people's affairs: enforce the law, and kinship is hurt by restraint;

sentences.zh: 厚族黨，則以偏私廢事；

translations.literal: if he favors clansmen, public duty is abandoned through partiality;
translations.idiomatic: favor the clan, and public duty is lost to partiality;

sentences.zh: 非古易地而官之道，當如鍾山議。

translations.literal: this is not the ancient way of exchanging offices by place—Bai Zhongshan's proposal should be followed.
translations.idiomatic: that is not the ancient principle of changing offices with the land. Bai Zhongshan's proposal should be adopted.

sentences.zh: 仍別設世襲六品官，選孔氏子充補。」

translations.literal: A separate hereditary sixth-rank office should still be established, filled by selection from Kong clansmen."
translations.idiomatic: A separate hereditary sixth-rank post should still be set up, filled by choosing Kong clansmen."

sentences.zh: 明製，五經博士，孔氏南宗一，奉衢州孔子廟祀；

translations.literal: Under the Ming system, Doctors of the Five Classics: one from the southern branch of the Kong clan, who attends sacrifice at the Quzhou Temple of Confucius;
translations.idiomatic: Under the Ming system there were Doctors of the Five Classics: one from the southern Kong line, who tended sacrifice at the Quzhou Temple of Confucius;

sentences.zh: 北宗一人，奉述聖祀。

translations.literal: one from the northern branch, who attends sacrifice to the Narrating Sage.
translations.idiomatic: and one from the northern line, who tended sacrifice to the Narrating Sage.

sentences.zh: 顏氏复聖後，曾氏宗聖後，孟氏亞聖後，仲氏子路後，各一人。

translations.literal: One each for the Yan clan, descendants of the Sage of Restitution; the Zeng clan, descendants of the Sage of Transmission; the Meng clan, descendants of the Second Sage; and the Zhong clan, descendants of Zilu.
translations.idiomatic: One each was appointed for the Yan house, heirs of the Restoring Sage; the Zeng house, heirs of the Transmitting Sage; the Meng house, heirs of the Second Sage; and the Zhong house, heirs of Zilu.

sentences.zh: 道州周氏元公後，江寧、嵩縣程氏皆正公後，洛陽邵氏康節後，建安、婺源硃氏皆文公後，各一人。

translations.literal: One each for the Zhou clan of Daozhou, descendants of Master Yuan; the Cheng clans of Jiangning and Song County, descendants of Master Zheng; the Shao clan of Luoyang, descendants of Master Kangjie; and the Zhu clans of Jian'an and Wuyuan, descendants of Master Wengong.
translations.idiomatic: One each for the Zhou of Daozhou, heirs of Master Yuan; the Cheng of Jiangning and Songxian, heirs of Master Zheng; the Shao of Luoyang, heirs of Master Kangjie; and the Zhu of Jian'an and Wuyuan, heirs of Master Wengong.

sentences.zh: 清因之。

translations.literal: The Qing followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing kept the same arrangement.

sentences.zh: 又增設咸陽姬氏文王后，曲阜東野氏周公後，濟寧閔氏子騫後，濬縣端木氏子貢後，常熟言氏子遊後，鉅野卜氏子夏后，蕭縣顓孫氏子張後，菏澤、肥城兩冉氏伯牛、仲弓後，肥城有氏有子後，鄒平伏氏伏生後，孟縣韓氏文公後，郿縣張氏明公後，各一人。

translations.literal: It also added: one each for the Ji clan of Xianyang, heirs of King Wen; the Dongye clan of Qufu, heirs of the Duke of Zhou; the Min clan of Jining, heirs of Ziqian; the Duanmu clan of Jun County, heirs of Zigong; the Yan clan of Changshu, heirs of Ziyou; the Bu clan of Juye, heirs of Zixia; the Zhuansun clan of Xiao County, heirs of Zizhang; the two Ran clans of Heze and Feicheng, heirs of Boniu and Zhonggong; the You clan of Feicheng, heirs of Youzi; the Fu clan of Zouping, heirs of Fusheng; the Han clan of Meng County, heirs of Master Wengong; and the Zhang clan of Mei County, heirs of Master Ming—one holder for each.
translations.idiomatic: It further added one post each for the Ji of Xianyang, heirs of King Wen; the Dongye of Qufu, heirs of the Duke of Zhou; the Min of Jining, heirs of Ziqian; the Duanmu of Junxian, heirs of Zigong; the Yan of Changshu, heirs of Ziyou; the Bu of Juye, heirs of Zixia; the Zhuansun of Xiaoxian, heirs of Zizhang; the two Ran lines of Heze and Feicheng, heirs of Boniu and Zhonggong; the You of Feicheng, heirs of Youzi; the Fu of Zouping, heirs of Fusheng; the Han of Mengxian, heirs of Master Wengong; and the Zhang of Meixian, heirs of Master Ming.

sentences.zh: 而程氏改純公後一人。

translations.literal: For the Cheng clan, this was changed to one descendant of Master Chungong.
translations.idiomatic: For the Cheng house the line was changed to a single heir of Master Chungong.

sentences.zh: 又崇關侯祀事，亦錄其後，洛陽、解州、江陵各一人。

translations.literal: Sacrifice to Lord Guan was also elevated, and his descendants were enrolled as well—one each at Luoyang, Jiezhou, and Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: The cult of Lord Guan was likewise honored, and his descendants were enrolled too—one at Luoyang, one at Jiezhou, and one at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 明史衍聖公附儒林傳後，今仿其例，並五經博士有增設者亦附焉。

translations.literal: The Ming History appended the Duke Yansheng after the biographies of Confucian scholars; we now follow that example, and also append here any additions made to the Doctors of the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming History placed the Duke Yansheng after the Confucian Scholars biographies; we follow that precedent here, and likewise append any new Doctors of the Five Classics established in our own time.
